---
title: "Leaf radiative transfer models as trait instruments"
---

```{python}
from _lib import *
ds = read("inventory_datasets")
em = read("error_model_comparison")
```

This site reports a Bayesian inversion of seven leaf radiative transfer models (RTMs) on a
harmonized library of leaf spectra with paired trait measurements. Most of the library comes
from EcoSIS, ECOSTRESS, NASA SHIFT and `spectra_db`. The models are PROSPECT-4, 5, 5B, D and
PRO, LIBERTY and LeafSIP. The work serves the manuscript *Chloroplasts to canopies*, and
results are organized around its two objectives:

* **A · How good are leaf RTMs?** Spectral fit, agreement between models, retrieval accuracy
  and calibration, out-of-sample transmittance, and where the models' assumptions break down
  (dried and ground samples, measurement protocols).
* **B · How do traits vary?** The best available trait estimate for every leaf, used for
  variance partitioning, treatment effects, and correlations within and across species.

## How it is built

* **Workflow.** Every step, from download to this site, is a Snakemake rule
  (`Snakefile`, `workflow/rules/`). Raw and processed data and fit results are not version
  controlled; the tables behind this site are published as a GitHub release asset.
* **Spectra are never resampled.** RTM output is mapped onto each spectrum's own wavelengths
  by an observation operator (selection, interpolation, or a spectral response function for
  coarse instruments).
* **Replicates and quantities.** All replicate spectra of a leaf, and both reflectance (R) and
  transmittance (T) where measured, enter one likelihood.
* **Error models.** Residuals are correlated across wavelengths, so iid errors make posteriors
  badly overconfident. Four structured error models are compared on the
  [Error models](error-models.qmd) page.
